_nota: Curiosidades del mapa mural (en inglés, como todo el mural). BORRADOR: falta verificar cifras con fuentes oficiales.

ave.texto: The bird. Five species, all flightless and mostly active at night. The only bird with nostrils at the tip of its bill: it finds worms by smell. Its egg is about 15% of the mother's weight. About 70,000 are left; where predators are not controlled, numbers fall about 2% a year.

fruta.texto: The fruit. It came from China as the “Chinese gooseberry”: Isabel Fraser brought the seeds in 1904. Growers renamed it “kiwifruit” in 1959 to sell it in the United States. Bay of Plenty grows most of the crop; Te Puke calls itself the kiwifruit capital of the world.

gente.texto: The people. New Zealanders have been “Kiwis” since World War I, when the bird on badges and on a popular boot polish gave the soldiers their nickname.

geografia.texto: The plate boundary runs 600 km along the Southern Alps, which rise about 10 mm a year. It last broke in 1717; a big quake in the next 50 years is likely (75%).
The lake fills a supervolcano. Its Oruanui eruption, 25,500 years ago, is the world's most recent supereruption.
GeoNet records about 20,000 a year; only 100 to 150 are big enough to be felt.
Milford Sound gets about 6,700 mm a year, one of the wettest places in the country.

slang: holiday home (crib in the far south)

historia.texto: Polynesian voyagers settle the islands: the ancestors of Māori.
Dutch navigator Abel Tasman reaches the coast.
James Cook lands at Gisborne and maps both islands.
The Treaty of Waitangi is signed at Waitangi, Bay of Islands, on 6 February, now Waitangi Day.
The first self-governing country where women can vote.
Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reach the top of Everest.
Te reo Māori becomes an official language.

mapa.texto: The largest living kauri tree: about 51 m tall and up to 2,500 years old.
The “glowworms” are larvae of a gnat found only in New Zealand; their light lures insects.
The Shire from The Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit films, open for tours.
Meet the kea, the world's only alpine parrot: clever and curious. Don't feed them.
The world's first commercial bungy jump, opened by AJ Hackett in 1988.
